questions.q: What does a "Pipeline" task type let one job task do?
options: Run an entire @dlt declarative pipeline — every table, in inferred dependency order — as a single step
Only run one specific @dlt.table function, never the whole pipeline
Replace the need for any job scheduling entirely
Only work with continuous mode pipelines, never triggered ones
questions.explain: This treats bronze, silver, and gold together as one unit, rather than three separate manually-chained tasks.

questions.q: Can a Lakeflow Job combine pipeline tasks with ordinary notebook tasks?
options: Yes — a notebook task can depend on a pipeline task finishing, for things like sending a notification after the pipeline completes
No, a job can only contain one type of task, never mixed
No, pipeline tasks must always run in a completely separate job
Only if Unity Catalog volumes are used for the notebook
questions.explain: This is the real, practical answer to coordinating work that isn't itself expressible as a @dlt.table.

questions.q: Why does orchestration still matter even with a fully declarative pipeline?
options: The declarative pipeline solves dependency ordering within itself, but not when it runs, what happens after, or how it relates to work outside any Lakeflow Pipeline
Declarative pipelines already handle all scheduling and post-run coordination automatically
Orchestration is entirely obsolete once a pipeline is declarative
Lakeflow Jobs only exists for pipelines that aren't declarative
questions.explain: This is where broader concerns like scheduling and coordinating with legacy notebooks or external calls still live.

questions.q: What is genuinely new in Lakeflow Jobs, versus what's simply renamed from Lesson 11?
options: The "Pipeline" task type itself — pointing a single task at an entire declarative pipeline, rather than only individual notebooks or scripts
The scheduling and run history concepts are entirely new, never covered before
Task dependency chains are a brand-new concept unrelated to Lesson 11
Nothing is new; Lakeflow Jobs is purely a rename with no new capability
questions.explain: Scheduling, task dependency chains, and run history are the same underlying job system under Lakeflow's current name.

questions.q: In the example job, what does Task 2 (send_notification) depend on?
options: Task 1 (run_pipeline) finishing successfully
Nothing — it runs independently and simultaneously with Task 1
Unity Catalog access control grants
The pipeline being set to continuous mode
questions.explain: This is exactly Lesson 11's task-chaining, now applied to a job containing a pipeline task type.
